cards.front: electricity
cards.back: A kind of energy that makes things work, such as lights and TVs.
cards.say: electricity. A kind of energy that makes things work, such as lights and TVs.

cards.front: battery
cards.back: A small store of electricity. It makes torches and toys work.
cards.say: battery. A small store of electricity. It makes torches and toys work.

cards.front: plug
cards.back: The part that goes into a socket.
cards.say: plug. The part that goes into a socket.

cards.front: socket
cards.back: The hole in the wall where we plug in a machine.
cards.say: socket. The hole in the wall where we plug in a machine.

cards.front: mains electricity
cards.back: Electricity from the wall socket. It can be very dangerous.
cards.say: mains electricity. Electricity from the wall socket. It can be very dangerous.

cards.front: Name something that uses electricity.
cards.back: A lamp, a TV, a fan or a fridge.
cards.say: Name something that uses electricity. A lamp, a TV, a fan or a fridge.

cards.front: Name something that uses a battery.
cards.back: A torch, a toy car or a clock.
cards.say: Name something that uses a battery. A torch, a toy car or a clock.

cards.front: Which is safe to play with: a battery toy or a wall socket?
cards.back: A battery toy. A wall socket is dangerous.
cards.say: Which is safe to play with: a battery toy or a wall socket? A battery toy. A wall socket is dangerous.

cards.front: Should you put your finger in a socket?
cards.back: No. It can hurt you badly.
cards.say: Should you put your finger in a socket? No. It can hurt you badly.

cards.front: Should you touch plugs with wet hands?
cards.back: No. Water and electricity are dangerous together.
cards.say: Should you touch plugs with wet hands? No. Water and electricity are dangerous together.

cards.front: Should you play near electric cables?
cards.back: No. Stay away from them.
cards.say: Should you play near electric cables? No. Stay away from them.

cards.front: Should you fly a kite near power lines?
cards.back: No. Stay far away from power lines.
cards.say: Should you fly a kite near power lines? No. Stay far away from power lines.

cards.front: Who should plug in machines?
cards.back: A grown up.
cards.say: Who should plug in machines? A grown up.

cards.front: What should you do if you see a broken cable?
cards.back: Stay away and tell a grown up.
cards.say: What should you do if you see a broken cable? Stay away and tell a grown up.

cards.front: Is it safe to pull a plug by its cable?
cards.back: No. Hold the plug itself.
cards.say: Is it safe to pull a plug by its cable? No. Hold the plug itself.

cards.front: Why should we switch off lights we do not need?
cards.back: It saves electricity.
cards.say: Why should we switch off lights we do not need? It saves electricity.

cards.front: Which uses electricity: a candle or a lamp?
cards.back: A lamp. A candle burns wax.
cards.say: Which uses electricity: a candle or a lamp? A lamp. A candle burns wax.

cards.front: Which needs no electricity: a pencil or a fan?
cards.back: A pencil.
cards.say: Which needs no electricity: a pencil or a fan? A pencil.

cards.front: Where does electricity from a wall socket come from?
cards.back: It comes from power stations through cables.
cards.say: Where does electricity from a wall socket come from? It comes from power stations through cables.

cards.front: Why should we not use electric things in the bath?
cards.back: Water and mains electricity are dangerous together.
cards.say: Why should we not use electric things in the bath? Water and mains electricity are dangerous together.

cards.front: Is it safe to play with batteries from a toy?
cards.back: No. Batteries should not be put in the mouth or taken apart.
cards.say: Is it safe to play with batteries from a toy? No. Batteries should not be put in the mouth or taken apart.

cards.front: Why is it good to turn off the TV when you leave a room?
cards.back: It saves electricity.
